subject: King of Kings Window Cleaning LLC — kingofkingswindowcleaning.com
rubric: Keystone v2, Part 10 — thirteen dimensions. NOT restated on v3.2; see rebaselining_rule.
build_track: 7A — greenfield static (Astro/Next on Vercel), replacing the live WordPress/Elementor install
average_basis: Eleven scored dimensions. Dimensions 12 and 13 are UNSCORED because neither has been measured, and Part 10 is explicit that they are scored from measurement, not from the survey — 'do not backfill it with an estimate.' Including them as zeros or as guesses would both be wrong; they are excluded from the mean and named as outstanding.
why_the_score_moved: Two dimensions were restated under changed v2 definitions and one under a newly written contract. Local fell from 3 to 1 because v2 redefines it as evidenced surface divided by claimed territory rather than raw lattice completeness — the 162 geo pages that earned a 3 for being complete now earn a 1 for being unevidenced. Convert fell from 3 to 2 because Part 4A finally specifies what Convert means, and the specification catches failures the old unspecified dimension could not. Nothing about the site changed between the two scores; the standard did.
target_basis: Eleven scored dimensions. Targets for 12 and 13 are set after the first measurement pass.
market_rank_current: 4th of 7 — unchanged, because every competitor was scored on the same eleven dimensions and none of them clears the v2 Local definition either. Mt. Baker's 175 geo pages are as unevidenced as King of Kings' 162.

dimensions.name: Services
dimensions.evidence: Eight service concepts sold (window, pressure washing, roof, moss, gutter, solar panel, house washing, commercial window). Five have a root hub; window cleaning — the flagship — has none: /window-cleaning-bellingham-wa/ is doing hub duty as a geo page. Hubs run 643-2,015 words. Zero problem-specific micro pages exist for problem-aware commercial intent.
dimensions.movement: Give every money service a real hub at /services/{service}/ built before its spokes (Part 3.1 cardinal rule), add the missing window-cleaning hub, split moss removal from moss prevention, and add the problem micro pages at /services/{service}/{problem}/. Nine hubs are now written and in band.

dimensions.name: Local
dimensions.v2_definition: Evidenced geographic surface divided by claimed territory. A geography correctly declined for lack of evidence costs nothing; a built page that cannot clear the substance gate costs a point.
dimensions.evidence: The live site claims 25 cities and builds 150 city x service pages plus 12 Bellingham neighborhood pages — 162 geo URLs. Measured against the v2 definition, the evidenced share of that surface is zero. Not one of the 162 declares three verifiable local specifics, carries a first-party proof from its own geography, or traces to a demand cluster; the demand map built on 2026-09-11 finds 0 of 328 geo slots clearing the Part 6A two-signal gate. The neighborhood tier additionally violates Part 3.4 item 4 outright — those 12 pages were built as the way into Bellingham, and the clause says neighborhood pages are built only inside cities that already rank, never as the way into a market. Under v1 this same surface scored 3, because v1 rewarded completeness. It is the same lattice; v2 asks a different question of it. MEASURED 2026-09-14, from the client's own 16-month Search Console export: the 150-page city x service lattice produced 388 impressions and 1 click in the entire window — 0.6% of the site's impressions and 0.1% of its clicks, at a median position of 41. 88 of the 150 were never shown once. Bellingham alone accounts for 21,409 of 31,164 query impressions (69%); every other market in the declared 25 returns fewer than 30 impressions over 16 months, and 33 of the 41 planned markets return nothing above noise. The v1 score of 3 was awarded for lattice completeness. The lattice is complete and it is invisible, which is the distinction v2's definition was written to capture.
dimensions.movement: Not 'build more geo pages.' Open the gate first: S5 job history from the client, then GSC. Then build only what clears it, with the substance gate enforced in the harness. A correctly declined geography costs nothing, so the honest end state may be materially fewer than 41 markets — and will score higher than 162 unevidenced pages do. The demand map now prunes on evidence rather than on judgement: 45 of 355 geo slots clear the two-signal gate — Bellingham across all seven services, plus nine other cities. The remaining 310 become areaServed mentions on their parent city page. A geography correctly declined costs nothing on this dimension.
dimensions.v3_2_note: v3.2 sharpens the decline exemption: "A geography declined for lack of job history is not a correct decline and does not earn the exemption — that cap is retired." Every decline in this build is on DEMAND evidence (no second signal), not on job history, so all 310 qualify as correct declines and cost nothing on this dimension.

dimensions.name: E-E-A-T
dimensions.evidence: No named expert anywhere on a service or geo page. The only Person nodes in the entire graph are blog authors. UBI 605476674 and 'Licensed / Insured / L&I' appear as visible text but are in no schema node — no hasCredential, no Person entity page, no first-person attribution. Five case studies exist (a genuine strength most of this market lacks) but they are not wired into the service spokes.
dimensions.movement: Randy Fee is now identified as the named expert and is wired into the build data layer with a two-part READY guard, so a named owner alone renders the expert block and hasCredential waits for a real registration number rather than blocking the name. Person entity page, author/reviewedBy references from Service and Article nodes, and every case study wired into its service spoke, city page and hub.

dimensions.name: Reviews
dimensions.evidence: 248 Google reviews is real, hard-won off-page authority and the second-strongest in the market. It is completely disconnected from the build: no aggregateRating, no LocalBusiness node to hang it on, no sameAs to the GBP or to the six social profiles the footer links out to.
dimensions.movement: Connect the entity — consistent NAP, sameAs to GBP and socials, correct business subtype — and pull aggregateRating from the verified GBP only, never hand-entered (Part 5.3). Ceiling stays 4 until review velocity is measured rather than assumed. v2 note: Part 10 now scores review incentives, gating and staff-written reviews under dimension 11, so the acquisition loop has to be designed clean, not just designed.

dimensions.name: Schema
dimensions.evidence: One JSON-LD emitter per page, which is correct and better than the two-emitter collision this portfolio has seen elsewhere. What it emits is the problem. A typical service page carries four nodes — WebPage, BreadcrumbList and two ListItems. Across all 287 URLs: zero LocalBusiness, zero Organization, zero Service, zero aggregateRating, zero sameAs. FAQPage appears on 6 of 287 pages. Nothing on this site tells a search engine what business this is. RESTATED: the v1 audit also counted zero SpeakableSpecification as a defect. v2 retires mandate M4 — Speakable never covered local-business pages, only news — so that is no longer a finding, and the emitter in the new build deliberately omits it.
dimensions.movement: Hand-built 7-node graph, one shared root #localbusiness @id declared once per domain and imported by every page, Service nodes on spokes, FAQPage on every URL from the same array the visible block renders, breadcrumbs mirroring the new taxonomy exactly.

dimensions.name: Content
dimensions.v2_change: REDEFINED — word floor retired, substance gate introduced
dimensions.evidence: 297,054 words across 287 URLs — a 1,035-word average, median 995. RESTATED: the v1 audit's headline content defect was that 286 of 287 pages sat under the 3,000-word M1 floor. v2 removes that floor as 'the one requirement in Keystone with no supporting evidence and material evidence against it,' and replaces it with per-type bands plus the four-item substance gate. Re-measured against the bands, the median city page at 995 words is INSIDE its 800-1,600 band, and most of the site's alleged thinness disappears. What does not disappear is the substance gate: zero of 287 pages declare three verifiable local specifics, zero carry a first-party proof from their own geography, zero carry a fact the top five competitors do not, and the 74-page duplicate H2 is a direct failure of item four. Structure is the other half — 73 blog posts in a chronological dump with six thin category pages, no cluster architecture, no surface library, no AEO Quick Answer on any page. Quality of the underlying research is genuinely good (Cherry Point fallout, Nooksack Valley farm dust, hard-water spotting), which is why this is a substantiation problem rather than a from-scratch one. MEASURED 2026-09-14: 138 of 287 URLs — 48% of the site — recorded zero impressions in 16 months. The homepage took 44% of page impressions and 79% of clicks; a 287-page site is performing as a one-page site. /roof-cleaning/ carries 5,125 impressions at average position 53.5 and /gutter-cleaning/ 4,781 at 57.5 — audiences already arriving at pages that cannot rank.
dimensions.movement: AEO Quick Answer block at the top of every page, reused as meta description and first FAQ answer. Pages written to band, not to a quota, with the four-item substance gate enforced as a build failure in the harness — which it now is, and which currently blocks the Ferndale exemplar for want of a real first-party proof. Consolidate the 73 posts into cluster posts each feeding exactly one service spoke. Build the Surface Library as the topical-authority backbone.

dimensions.name: Design
dimensions.evidence: Clean, consistent Elementor build on hello-elementor from the 180sites.com template stable. Mobile-workable, click-to-call present. It reads as a template because it is one — nothing in the visual system is specific to this brand.
dimensions.movement: A real named palette and type system as CSS variables, brand hero and logo on every page (M7), field photography as the visual anchor rather than stock.

dimensions.name: Convert
dimensions.v2_change: NEWLY SPECIFIED — Part 4A, the Conversion Contract
dimensions.evidence: RESTATED DOWNWARD, on the site as it was already measured. v1 scored this 3 against an unwritten standard; v2 Part 4A exists because 'a build that ranks and does not convert is a failure the scorecard could previously mark as a 4.' Against the written contract: 4A.1 requires exactly one declared primary action per page, and the primary offer here is an H2 — 'Try Bellingham's Best Window Washing Risk-Free' on 74 pages — competing with the click-to-call for the same visual weight, so the primary action is ambiguous by construction. 4A.2 requires a guarantee with terms; there is no /our-guarantee/ page on the domain. There is no financing page. The CTA is a sitewide banner rather than named per market. Genuinely better than the market on the basics: click-to-call, a five-second quote promise, a Square checkout path, a referral programme. NOT MEASURED, and therefore not counted against the score: form field count against the five-field limit, GA4 call and form conversion events, the #:~:text= custom dimension, AI-referrer segmentation, and whether a call-tracking number has displaced the GBP number in the footer NAP or the schema node (4A.3). Those five are the first things to check, and any of them could move this score in either direction.
dimensions.movement: One declared primary action per page in the data row. Risk-free offer rendered from a CTA component instead of a duplicated heading. Real /our-guarantee/ terms page. Financing page with a live calculator. GA4 attribution shipped as part of the build, not after it — including the #:~:text= dimension, without which roughly 22% of AI-Overview citation clicks misattribute to Direct.

dimensions.name: Performance
dimensions.v2_gate: LCP <= 2.0s, TBT <= 200ms, CLS <= 0.05, Lighthouse >= 90, median of five runs, mobile; LCP image in initial HTML with fetchpriority; JS < 300KB; images sized; HTML under 2MB; field re-check at 28 days.
dimensions.evidence: Measured logged-out on /window-cleaning-ferndale-wa/: TTFB 149ms, DOM interactive 362ms, load 595ms — the WP Rocket cache is doing its job. Payload is the weakness: 96 requests and 707KB, of which 486KB is CSS (Elementor + Elementor Pro + Premium Addons Pro). Only 75 of 2,277 image elements sitewide are WebP (3.3%), and the sampled page lazy-loads none of its 13 images, though all 13 carry explicit width and height. HONESTY NOTE: navigation timings are not the v2 lab gate. No Lighthouse median-of-five mobile run has been performed, so LCP, TBT, CLS and the score are unmeasured and this 3 rests on payload discipline and server response alone. It is provisional in both directions.
dimensions.movement: Static output kills the 486KB of builder CSS outright. WebP with explicit dimensions, LCP image in the initial HTML with fetchpriority, lazy-load below the fold. Run the median-of-five mobile lab gate before launch and again in the field at 28 days — v2 makes both a gate, not a phase.
dimensions.v3_2_note: v3.2 names INP as the field metric, distinct from lab TBT: "a passing TBT does not imply a passing INP, and on page-builder themes they diverge routinely." The 28-day field re-check is now INP <= 200ms, run with Vercel Optimize where the site is on Vercel. Neither has been measured here, so this 3 remains provisional.

dimensions.name: Integrity
dimensions.evidence: Strong on the basics — exactly one H1 on all 287 pages, zero orphans, zero duplicate titles, zero canonical mismatches, zero noindex accidents, zero non-200s, zero JSON-LD parse errors. Wrecked by two things. First, taxonomy: 275 of 287 URLs are flat root-level slugs, one up to 113 characters; there is no /services/ or /locations/ directory, so no hierarchy exists for authority to flow through. Second, cannibalization: Bellingham window cleaning is targeted simultaneously by /window-cleaning-bellingham-wa/, /window-cleaning-cost-bellingham-wa/, /what-affects-the-cost-of-professional-window-cleaning-in-bellingham-and-surrounding-areas/, /professional-window-cleaning-services-in-bellingham-surrounding-areas/, /the-complete-guide-to-professional-window-cleaning-in-bellingham-wa/ and several more. 'Try Bellingham's Best Window Washing Risk-Free' as an H2 on 74 pages is the Part 12.1 repeated-exact-match-H2 signature. Cannibalization is now confirmed in performance data rather than inferred from the crawl: /services/pressure-washing/ (1,420 impressions, position 32.2) and /pressure-washing/ (356, position 43.2) are both live and both accruing impressions for the same intent.
dimensions.movement: Impose the Part 3.3 taxonomy with page-by-page 301s (197 mapped), consolidate each duplicated intent to one canonical page, and render the repeated heading from a CTA component so it stops being a heading at all. v2 adds the prevention layer the v1 harness lacked: scripts/keyword-map-check.mjs now fails the wave on a (service, geo) tuple claimed by two URLs, so this specific failure cannot recur in the new build.

dimensions.name: Honesty & compliance
dimensions.evidence: Nothing fabricated — no invented aggregateRating, no fake pricing, no phantom credentials, NAP consistent across the site, single-entity site with no cross-brand bleed. Two real violations of doctrine #6: 'Risk-Free' is used as an unqualified guarantee on 74 pages with no terms page anywhere on the domain, and 'Bellingham's Best' is an unsubstantiated superiority claim in a heading. The UBI is published, which is legitimate public record but should be a documented client decision (Part 8). NOT MEASURED: v2 adds review incentives, review gating and staff-written reviews to this dimension. Nothing observed suggests any of the three, but nothing observed rules them out either — this needs a direct conversation with the client, not an inference from the site.
dimensions.movement: Every 'guaranteed' and 'risk-free' string links to /our-guarantee/ with defined terms — blocked on Randy supplying the actual terms, and /our-guarantee/ is noindex until he does. 'Bellingham's Best' is already replaced in the build by a substantiated claim drawn from the client's own awards page, with dates. Confirm UBI publication in writing.
dimensions.v3_2_note: v3.2 reworded "credentials real" to the client-attested standard and RETIRED verification as a publish blocker. Nothing ships gated on independent verification. What replaces it: record who supplied a fact and when, mark it attested in the guardrail file, and never invent. The honesty doctrine is untouched — fabrication is still barred, and an attestation is not a fabrication. Randy's territory-wide job history is the live example: attested, recorded, used.

dimensions.name: Entity & off-site presence
dimensions.what_is_scored: GBP completeness — primary category, hours including holidays, keyword-bearing predefined services, service areas within the 20 limit, photo recency, the address-visibility decision. A citation core of 30-50 mainstream plus vertical directories, not 500. Unlinked brand mentions. Presence on the third-party platforms LLMs draw on for local queries.
dimensions.why_unscored: None of it has been measured. The GBP has not been audited, no citation sweep has been run, and no brand-mention scan exists. Part 10 says to score 12 and 13 from measurement and explicitly warns against backfilling with an estimate, so this stays blank rather than becoming a plausible 3.
what_is_known_without_scoring: 248 Google reviews exist, so a GBP exists and is active.
Six social profiles are linked from the site footer — the off-page half of the entity is partly built already.

The Secretary of State principal office address is residential, which makes the address-visibility decision a real decision rather than a default, and it is why streetAddress stays null in the build data.
Whatcom County service-area coverage against the 20-service-area GBP limit is untested against the 41 declared markets — the declared territory already exceeds what a GBP can express.

Citation sweep across the 30-50 core: NAP character-consistency against the GBP, not against the website.
Presence check on the third-party platforms that surface in local assistant answers.

the service-area-business decision, decided once and applied identically
v3_2_citation_core.status_here: Only the GBP has been read. Tier 1 is otherwise unaudited, tiers 2-4 untouched. The address-visibility decision is open and is the live sub-item — see archive/gbp-findings.json GBP-1.

dimensions.name: AI answer surface
dimensions.what_is_scored: Measured presence across a fixed prompt set — service x city x intent, held constant per client — in AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT and Perplexity. GSC generative-AI impression trend. Named-mention versus ghost-citation split.
dimensions.why_unscored: No prompt set has been run. A score here without a run would be exactly the fabrication the standard forbids.
what_is_known_without_scoring: MEASURED 2026-09-11: kingofkingswindowcleaning.com/robots.txt allows every AI crawler. It contains one User-agent: * group disallowing only /wp-admin/, plus the sitemap line. GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot and Bytespider are all permitted. There is no access problem to fix — the surface is reachable and simply has nothing on it worth citing.

MEASURED 2026-09-11: whatcomgrc.com blocks anthropic-ai, AI2Bot, Ai2Bot-Dolma, aiHitBot, Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended and Bytespider by name. One of the seven competitors has voluntarily removed itself from assistant answers.

Vercel's crawler study finds GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Meta's crawler fetch JavaScript but do not execute it. The 7A static track therefore serves NAP, services, reviews and the Quick Answer in initial HTML by construction, which the current Elementor build does not guarantee.

Steady Demand's 86,645-citation study finds AI Overviews cite the business's own website 70.7% of the time while AI Mode cites Google Maps / GBP 79.8% — so dimension 13 cannot be moved by the site alone, and dimension 12 is half of its remedy.
first_measurement_pass: Fix a prompt set — service x city x intent — and freeze it, so the trend is comparable quarter over quarter.
Run it across AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT and Perplexity; record named-mention versus ghost-citation.
Wire the GSC generative-AI report and the GA4 #:~:text= custom dimension before launch, not after — without the latter roughly 22% of AI-Overview citation sessions misattribute to Direct.

v3_2_citability_subscore.rule: v3.2 adds an input sub-score to this dimension: the share of indexable pages carrying all four Part 6.5 citability signals, and the share carrying their declared snippet shape in real markup (Part 4.3). Presence is the outcome and lags; citability is the input and can be scored on day one. Never average the input into the outcome to flatter the number.
v3_2_citability_subscore.measured_2026_09_14: 0 of 25 pages carry all four signals; 5 carry three or more. 25 of 25 carry their declared snippet shape in real markup.
v3_2_citability_subscore.instrument: scripts/citability.mjs, wired into npm run verify.

dimensions.name: Accessibility
dimensions.what_is_scored: Operable without a mouse and legible without perfect vision: keyboard reachability and order, a visible :focus-visible state everywhere, real <label> or aria-label on every control plus autocomplete and a meaningful name, labelled icon-only buttons, semantic elements for their job (never <div onClick>), WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large) with colour never the only carrier of meaning, tap targets >= 44x44px with touch-action: manipulation, link text descriptive out of context, prefers-reduced-motion honoured, correct alt with alt="" on decorative images, and usable at 200% zoom and 320px.
dimensions.how_it_is_run: Per TEMPLATE, not per page. A finding on a template blocks that template's first publish as a P0.
dimensions.rule_source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines, referenced not copied (Part 16.5) — fetched fresh at run time, because a pasted copy is stale within a month.
dimensions.status_here: Seven components and three layouts exist and none has been audited. This is the one dimension that can be moved entirely by us, with no client input and no measurement window — which makes it the cheapest outstanding item on the rubric.

rebaselining_rule.standard: Keystone v3.1/v3.2, Part 10: "never restate a historical score on a newer rubric — state the rubric version with every score quoted."
rebaselining_rule.what_this_means_here: The 2.27 average on this page is a KEYSTONE v2 SCORE and stays labelled as one. It is not converted to v3.2 and must not be quoted as a v3.2 number. v3.2 adds Dimension 14 (Accessibility), redefines the Dimension 2 decline exemption, adds a citability sub-score to Dimension 13 and names the citation core in Dimension 12 — a v3.2 figure requires a fresh scoring pass against those definitions, not arithmetic on this one.
rebaselining_rule.note_on_the_earlier_restatement: This file previously restated the v1 score of 2.55 as 2.27 on the v2 rubric. v3 now forbids exactly that move. The v2 restatement stands as history because it was made under v2, and no further restatement will be made.
rebaselining_rule.next_score: A v3.2 scoring pass is outstanding and is listed in the open items below.

open_items_v3_2: Run a v3.2 scoring pass across all fourteen dimensions. The 2.27 on this page is a v2 score and may not be converted.
Accessibility audit per template (7 components, 3 layouts) against the Web Interface Guidelines — blocks first publish of each template.
Backfill Part 6.5 citability on the 20 pages that do not yet carry all four signals.

Dimension 13 measurement per the new 10.4 methodology: 3-5 runs per prompt with the rate reported against its sample size, fan-out query extraction, three-way cause split, visibility ladder, branded search as the attribution basis.
Citation core audit — Tier 1 beyond the GBP, then Tier 2 aggregators.
Part 3.5 navigation shell specification, including the Nav Location column in the keyword-URL map.
Segment pages (the ninth page type) — [service] for [segment], orthogonal to (service, geo).
Segmented XML sitemaps by page type; writer-register scanner as the eighth harness script.
GA4 measurement hygiene per 16.6 — retention set past the two-month default, internal traffic excluded, referral exclusions, no summing of platform-claimed conversions.
